However, all five posttonic vowels are subject to syncope in proparoxytones, because a prosodic constraint banning proparoxytones outranks the phonological rule that preserves atonic [a] [...]"; p. 121: "Thus, original proparoxytones yield oxytones (> 1ζ) in varieties such as Forlivese [...] southeast of the Marecchia syncope of original proparoxytones yields paroxytones with a paragogic vowel (> 1ζ2ζ), as typified by Sammarinese [...]". new_statements.translation: Ercolani: 'The tonic accent, if not indicated by special marks, always falls on the last syllable.'

new_statements.rule_in_words: Inherited Romance lexical stress, but confined to the last two syllables: loss of all final unstressed vowels except -a makes most words consonant-final oxytones (gat, cavàl, sumar), words in -a are paroxytone (cavala, amiga), and antepenult stress is excluded by a productive ban on proparoxytones (old proparoxytones become C-final paroxytones like fóran/sàbet via epenthesis, oxytones via syncope, or paroxytones with a paragogic vowel in San Marino); a lexical residue of vowel-final oxytones (tumarà, avnù, piò, apocopated infinitives cantê) and C-final paroxytones means position is not fully predictable from word shape, which is why the orthographies mark exactly those cases.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Michelotti marks secondary stress in transcriptions (e.g. [ˈljɛviˌto], p. xix) and reconstructs historical secondary-stress patterns (1ζ2ζζ north vs 1ζζ2ζ southeast of the Marecchia, p. 121) but states no synchronic secondary-stress rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Sammarinese sporadically restores etymological posttonic vowels in a few lexicalised items (sàbet, ståmmeg, Rèmmin; Vitali & Pioggia 2010: 11; Michelotti p. 122); numerals 11-16 oscillate between forms with and without paragogic vowel; proclitic words (sèmpar, tânt, zent) lose or weaken their stress onto the following word (Casadio, la Ludla sett. 2006 p. 10).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (citation forms); Michelotti notes the proparoxytone ban and the ban on heavy atonic final syllables also operate over the prosodic word verb+enclitic (pp. 204-205, 422, 447); Vitali 2008 notes long/open-mid vowels always bear word stress but can be de-stressed in the phrase.
new_statements.identity_note: Michelotti 2008 is fieldwork-based on Sammarinese (dialects of the Republic of San Marino, which he classes as 'Borderline Romagnol'), but the quoted ch. 1-2 statements are framed for the Romagnol group as a whole and explicitly contrast Central Romagnol (Forlì/Ravenna plain, the 'rf' koiné of Vitali) with Sammarinese; both fall under Glottolog roma1328 (countries IT; SM), no separate glottocode for Sammarinese known to me. Ercolani [1960] and Lapucci 1986 describe the Ravenna-Forlì plain varieties. Pesarese (Vitali & Pioggia ch. 36, also saved) is Gallo-Italic of the Marche, not Romagnol proper, and was not used.

sources.note: No positional rule stated; stress treated as inherited. States apocope of all final vowels except [a] and a prosodic constraint banning proparoxytones (pp. 20-21); Central Romagnol original proparoxytones > oxytones, Sammarinese > paroxytones with paragogic vowel (pp. 121-122); ban on proparoxytones and on heavy atonic word-final syllables is synchronically productive in verb+enclitic words (pp. 204-205, 422, 447). Transcription marks primary and secondary stress (p. xix).

sources.citation: Lapucci, Mario (ed.). 1986. Regole fondamentali di grafia romagnola. Ravenna: Edizioni del Girasole. §III Accenti, pp. 15-16.
sources.note: Orthographic norm: accent not written on tronche ending in consonant (amstir, sumar), piane ending in vowel (cavala, figura), monosyllables; written on tronche ending in vowel (tumarà, murì, sustnù), piane ending in consonant (disàstar, zócul) and sdrucciole (pìgura, scótula) - i.e. default final stress for C-final and penult for V-final words, with lexical exceptions.

sources.citation: Ercolani, Libero. [1960]. Vocabolario romagnolo-italiano. Ravenna: Monte di Ravenna. (front matter 'Valori fonetici', p. XIII-XIV)
sources.note: 'L'accento tonico, se non è indicato con segni particolari, cade sempre sull'ultima sillaba.' Also: in infinitives with final-syllable stress the final -r is mute.

sources.citation: Schürr, Friedrich. 1919. Romagnolische Dialektstudien II: Lautlehre lebender Mundarten. Sitzungsberichte Akad. Wiss. Wien, phil.-hist. Kl. 188/1.
sources.note: Historical Lautlehre organised by Latin accent class (Paroxytona/Proparoxytona/Oxytona); remarks on falling diphthongs being grounded in the 'gesamten Akzentverhältnisse' (p. 36) and on accent retraction within diphthongs; no synchronic word-stress placement statement.

sources.citation: Istituto Friedrich Schürr. n.d. Norme ortografiche dell'Istituto Friedrich Schürr. 1 p.
sources.note: Grave accent marks tonic position in sdrucciole (pìgura), piane ending in consonant (fòran) and tronche ending in vowel (piò); otherwise unmarked.

sources.note: Full stressed/unstressed vowel inventories; all final unstressed vowels other than -a lost (gat, cavàl, öm); former proparoxytones repaired by epenthesis (rf fóran, védar) or epithesis (riminese fórne, védre; sars. fórni). No positional stress rule.

sources.citation: Vitali, Daniele. 2008. L'ortografia romagnola. Cesena: Il Ponte Vecchio / Associazione Istituto Friedrich Schürr. 45 pp.
sources.note: §2.8: proposes writing the accent always except when it falls on the penult of a vowel-final word (cavàl, cavala, furmìg, furmiga); notes rf caval is 'un bisillabo con l'ultima vocale accentata lunga'; §1: /eː oː ɛː ɔː ɛ ɔ/ occur only under word stress. No positional rule.

sources.citation: Casadio, Gilberto. 2006-2009. Appunti di grammatica storica del dialetto romagnolo I-XXVI. la Ludla (Istituto F. Schürr), esp. VI 'Vocalismo atono', gennaio 2007 p. 9; XX giugno 2008 p. 9.
sources.note: Historical: unstressed vowels other than a fall totally, attributed to the strong intensity of the tonic accent; 'spostamento dell'accento' only for IE/IO nexus (FILIOLU > fiôl). No synchronic placement rule.

sources.citation: Schürr, Friedrich. 1917. Romagnolische Mundarten. Sprachproben in phonetischer Transkription. Sitzungsberichte Akad. Wiss. Wien, phil.-hist. Kl. 181/2.
sources.note: Transcription intro discusses tempo, Druck and Ton affecting stressed-vowel quantity/quality; no placement rule.
